findings.problem: The degree-plus-rows bookkeeping proof is repeated three times: here for sameLeft (116-137), for sameRight (215-237), and in the base file's `satisfiesTransmission_wedgeAddDivisor_iff_profile`. All three do the same thing: split the conjunction, rewrite the degree with `deg_wedgeAddDivisor` and `genus_vertexWedge`, and transport the `∀ a b, TransmissionInequality ↔ ∀ ell, Row` equivalence through the conjunction. Only the marked vertices and the row predicate differ. Each new marking configuration would need another copy.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma in TransmissionWedge.lean, or at the top of this file, generic in the marked vertices and the row predicate. Its statement would be: for `u v : (vertexWedge G H x y).V`, `Row : ℤ → ℤ → ℤ → Prop`, and `hRow : ∀ a b, TransmissionInequality (vertexWedge G H x y) u v tau (wedgeAddDivisor G H x y D E) a b ↔ ∀ ell, Row a b ell`, we have `SatisfiesTransmission (vertexWedge G H x y) u v tau (wedgeAddDivisor G H x y D E) ↔ CFDiv.degree D + CFDiv.degree E = genus G + genus H + tau.χ ∧ ∀ a b ell, Row a b ell`. The proof is the existing `constructor` block, with `hRow a b` in place of the per-case iff. The same-left theorem then becomes `satisfiesTransmission_wedgeAddDivisor_iff_of_rows _ _ (fun a b ell => WedgeSameLeftTransmissionRowProfile G H x y D E p q tau a b ell) (transmissionInequality_wedgeAddDivisor_sameLeft_iff_rowProfile G H x y D E p q tau)`. The same-right theorem and the base theorem become the analogous one-line instances. The target types are definitionally the same as the current statements, because `WedgeSame*TransmissionProfile` unfolds to the right-hand side.
findings.benefit: One copy of the degree/genus and row-transport argument replaces three. Each case then only states its row predicate and its row iff, which is the real content. Changes to `SatisfiesTransmission` or to the wedge degree lemmas are made once, and new marking cases cost a single line.

findings.problem: Four `have` blocks (`hP` and `hQ` in each of the two twist lemmas, at 66-75 and 163-174) re-prove that `n • oneChip` of a lifted vertex equals the wedge lift of `n • oneChip`. Each rewrites with `wedgeAddDivisor_one_chip_*`, then `wedgeAddDivisor_zsmul`, then `simp`. The base lemma `wedgeAddDivisor_transmissionTwist` (TransmissionWedge.lean 113-123) has the same two blocks again, so there are six copies in total. The closing step `rw [hP, hQ, wedgeAddDivisor_add, wedgeAddDivisor_sub]; simp` is also repeated three times.
findings.proposed_change: In TransmissionWedge.lean, after `wedgeAddDivisor_one_chip_right`, add two lemmas: `smul_oneChip_inl_eq_wedgeAddDivisor (n : ℤ) (u : G.V) : n • oneChip (G := vertexWedge G H x y) (Sum.inl u) = wedgeAddDivisor G H x y (n • oneChip u) 0` and `smul_oneChip_wedgeRightVertex_eq_wedgeAddDivisor (n : ℤ) (v : H.V) : n • oneChip (G := vertexWedge G H x y) (wedgeRightVertex G H x y v) = wedgeAddDivisor G H x y 0 (n • oneChip v)`. Their proofs are the existing `rw [← wedgeAddDivisor_one_chip_*, wedgeAddDivisor_zsmul]; simp` blocks. Both twist lemmas here, and the base twist lemma, then become `rw [smul_oneChip_inl_eq_wedgeAddDivisor, smul_oneChip_inl_eq_wedgeAddDivisor, wedgeAddDivisor_add, wedgeAddDivisor_sub]; simp` (or the right-vertex analogue). The `hP`/`hQ` blocks and their duplicated statements with the explicit `(G := vertexWedge G H x y)` annotation disappear. The two lemmas are stated with the same hypotheses as the current `hLeft`/`hRight`, so no extra imports are needed.
findings.benefit: Each chip-lifting argument is proved once and named, instead of six times with repeated long type ascriptions. The twist lemmas shrink to their actual content, which is how the twist splits across factors. Any change to `wedgeAddDivisor_one_chip_*` or `wedgeAddDivisor_zsmul` needs one edit instead of six.
